actions.text: Received in the Senate. Read twice. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 467.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H5159)

At the conclusion of debate, the chair put the question on the motion to suspend the rules. Mr. Burlison objected to the vote on the grounds that a quorum was not present. Further proceedings on the motion were postponed. The point of no quorum was considered as withdrawn.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 1722.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H4663-4664; text: CR H4663)
Mr. Burlison moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended.
Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 39 - 0.
Committee Consideration and Mark-up Session Held

Referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, and in addition to the Committee on Armed Services, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal executive agencies, independent regulatory agencies, contractors, and congressional oversight committees.
dimensions.evidence: the term covered agency means an Executive agency... and an independent regulatory agency

dimensions.assessment: Imposes administrative reporting and oversight requirements rather than altering project execution directly.
dimensions.evidence: issue guidance requiring covered agencies to, on an annual basis, submit to the Director information

dimensions.assessment: No new direct project funding is authorized; administrative costs are absorbed within existing agency operations.
Applies broadly across all federal agencies and major time-limited projects meeting delay or cost-overrun thresholds.
dimensions.evidence: require an annual report of taxpayer-funded projects that are over budget and behind schedule

dimensions.assessment: Establishes an ongoing, permanent annual reporting requirement for federal agencies.
dimensions.evidence: submit to the Director and post on the website... an annual report

importance_detail.rationale: This bill requires federal executive and independent agencies to submit annual reports to the OMB and Congress regarding major projects that are significantly delayed or over budget.
